principle: MEASURE THE CLOCK BEFORE MEASURING THE LAG

local_clock.notes: No NTP/clock-offset measurement was ever recorded by the recorder (estimated_clock_offset_ms is null). Receive-minus-source values therefore mix true transport delay with an unknown local clock offset and MUST NOT be decomposed into the two. No retroactive clock correction is applied to any raw or derived timestamp.

entries.origin: Binance matching engine; field T of wss://stream.binance.com:9443/ws/btcusdt@trade trade messages; parsed by std0_quant.collectors.btc_ticks.parse_binance_trade as int(message['T'])
entries.evidence: Collector code maps T directly (src/std0_quant/collectors/btc_ticks.py parse_binance_trade); module docstring documents 'Binance trade time (T)'; observed E-T p50 = 1ms across raw files, consistent with engine-stamped trade times.
entries.notes: Trade execution time on the Binance server clock. Cross-source ordering against Polymarket timestamps is LIMITED: the Binance<->Polymarket server clock offset is unknown and was never measured.

entries.origin: Binance event dispatch time; field E of the trade message; parsed by parse_binance_trade as int(message.get('E') or message['T'])
entries.evidence: Collector code maps E directly; E-T p50 = 1ms observed in raw (engine dispatch follows execution within ~1ms).
entries.notes: Not used as a lead-lag basis in phase2b research; recorded so the E-vs-T distinction stays explicit.

entries.origin: Local clock via std0_quant.timeutil.utc_now_ms() = int(time.time()*1000), captured once per websocket text frame at on_text entry in TickRecorder._on_text
entries.evidence: Collector passes self._clock() (=utc_now_ms) into handle_binance_text per frame (src/std0_quant/collectors/btc_ticks.py _on_text). collect_live.py runs the BTC and Polymarket recorders in ONE asyncio loop via asyncio.gather; identical-millisecond receive bursts were measured in raw (median 8.77 rows per identical ms, max 94) while the Polymarket stream runs ~900 events/s, proving burst quantization by the shared loop.
entries.notes: Same local clock as polymarket_clob receive timestamps, so cross-source RECEIVE-time ordering is possible; ordering of rows inside one identical-ms burst is NOT resolvable.

entries.origin: Polymarket CLOB websocket market-channel payload field 'timestamp'; parsed by std0_quant.collectors.polymarket_book.parse_ts_to_ms(message.get('timestamp')) in BookState._row
entries.evidence: Advances ~306 distinct values/s (per-frame rate, not per-trade); frozen spans (identical timestamp across consecutive frames) max 259ms; overlap with last_trade_price event times only 0.9%, proving it is NOT last-trade time; batched price_changes[] children all inherit the parent frame timestamp (collector expands children with the same exchange_timestamp_ms; raw_message_ref/frame_id groups them).
entries.notes: DO NOT call this exchange trade time. It is the per-frame server timestamp: event-level ordering inside one frame is impossible, intra-frame spread is bounded by observed frozen spans (<=259ms), and it is NOT the execution time of any order. Cross-source ordering vs BTC event time is LIMITED (frame vs event semantics plus unknown server clock offset).

entries.origin: Local clock via utc_now_ms(), captured once per websocket text frame at on_text entry (BookState handle path receives receive_ts_ms per frame; every derived child row of one frame shares it)
entries.evidence: Collector code captures receive_ts once per frame; all price_changes[] children of one frame carry the identical receive_timestamp_ms in raw.
entries.notes: Same local clock as binance_btc receive timestamps; one receive stamp per frame (frame-level granularity).

entries.origin: Computed by research code (never recorded by the collector): max(receive_timestamp_ms of all raw events needed to construct that book state). For collector phase2a_prospective_v4 this equals the receive timestamp of the constructing frame, because the book is reconstructed synchronously in the same loop that stamps receive time.
entries.evidence: No separate LOCAL_PROCESS_TIME is recorded (process_ts stays null in timing diagnostics); availability == constructing event receive_ts verified per market by the v3 pipeline's no-backdating check.
entries.notes: HARD RULE: state availability can never precede the local receive time of any construction input (no backdating). This is a research-computed field, so every use is guarded by validate_no_backdating.

entries.origin: Polymarket data-API std0 fills (Phase 2A prospective cohort); second-granularity timestamps
entries.evidence: Phase 2A/2B frozen B2 rule: same-second millisecond ordering is FORBIDDEN; post-fill anchor is fill_second_end.
entries.notes: Second-level only. B2 timing resolution carries >=1s ambiguity by construction and can never validate a 250ms reaction claim.
